definition_tex:
\subsection{Definitions and mathematical statement}
\paragraph{Shared notation.}$\mathbb N$, $\mathbb Z$, $\mathbb Q$, $\mathbb R$, and $\mathbb C$ denote the natural numbers, integers, rationals, reals, and complex numbers, respectively. All additional parameters and hypotheses are specified in the question.


\paragraph{Statement recorded in the supplied source.}
Is there a rationally connected irrational variety $X$ with property (*)?

Recall Property (*) from a previous question was defined as follows.
\[
D(X) = \langle \mathscr A_1, \ldots, \mathscr A_m \rangle
\]
has a semiorthogonal decomposition
with $\mathscr A_i \hookrightarrow D(Y_i)$ such that ${\rm dim} Y_i \leq {\rm dim}X-2.$
\par\smallskip\textit{Formulation references:} \href{https://huggingface.co/datasets/ulamai/UnsolvedMath}{[S1]}, \href{http://aimpl.org/rationalityag/1/}{[S2]}.

\subsection{Short English statement}
Is there a rationally connected irrational variety $X$ with property (*)?

Recall Property (*) from a previous question was defined as follows.
\[
D(X) = \langle \mathscr A_1, \ldots, \mathscr A_m \rangle
\]
has a semiorthogonal decomposition
with $\mathscr A_i \hookrightarrow D(Y_i)$ such that ${\rm dim} Y_i \leq {\rm dim}X-2.$
